# Linked sizes, in BYTES, of the self-host driver binaries CI already builds —
# checked against every run by scripts/ci-check-driver-sizes (#6826).
#
# WHICH BINARY IS "THE SELF-HOST BINARY": fern.fern, named below as the tracked
# artifact. It is examples/self_host/fern.fern, the whole self-hosted compiler
# CLI, and it is the number to quote when talking about self-host binary size
# (#4109's "well under half" target is against it). The others in this file are
# smaller programs that link a SUBSET of the compiler: `asm_ir_run` is the
# front-end plus the x86-64 IR backend, `wasm_ir_run` the front-end plus the
# wasm one, and so on. They are recorded because they are free to record and
# they localise a regression to a backend — NOT because they are
# interchangeable. Quoting one against another is how #4109 acquired a bogus
# "the epic is 4x off": a 245 MB CLI figure compared with a 59 MB wasm_ir_run
# figure.
#
# tracked-artifact: fern.fern
#
# HOW THIS IS MEASURED. Nothing extra is built. Every driver here is linked by
# the `warm` / `cli` jobs of test-e2e-selfhost.yml on their own account;
# TestSelfHostWarmStockDriver stats each one it warms into
# FERN_DRIVER_SIZE_REPORT, and the job compares that report against this file.
# The emit and the link are in-process pure Go, so a given commit yields the
# same byte count on any runner — a difference here is a real change in the
# compiler's output, not runner noise.
#
# TWO THRESHOLDS, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Drift past FERN_SIZE_TOLERANCE_PERCENT
# (5%) is a job-summary line plus a warning annotation; drift past
# FERN_SIZE_FAIL_PERCENT (15%) FAILS the `driver-sizes` job, which is where the
# check runs as a gate rather than as a report. A SHRINK counts as drift too: an
# un-updated baseline after a win silently raises the ceiling the next
# regression is measured against, which is how 16% of growth went unnoticed for
# eight days.
#
# The two numbers are far apart because ordinary work moves these binaries more
# than one might guess. Between the 2026-08-14 baseline below and 08-15 — one
# day, ~60 commits, nothing about it unusual — every driver grew, the
# whole-compiler ones by ~3.0% and the 6 MB front-end slices by ~7%. A 5% gate
# would have reddened twelve of fifteen on an ordinary day; a 15% one is still
# well under the +16.1% / +31.4% event this file exists for.
#
# WHEN A NUMBER MOVES ON PURPOSE, update it in the same PR — the job summary
# prints the corrected lines ready to paste. Keep the reason in the PR, not
# here; this file is a set of current facts.
#
# x86-64. The `warm` and `cli` jobs are x86-only (the aarch64 lane skips the x86
# driver builds), so there is one architecture to baseline and no per-arch split.
#
# Measured 2026-08-15 on origin/main 83391754e, off-CI, through the same
# in-process emit + assemble + link the `warm` / `cli` jobs use. The previous
# figures were CI's own (run 31782687541) and the three #6826 measured off-CI
# agreed with them to within 0.05% — fern.fern 155,895,596 vs 155,973,500,
# asm_ir_run 146,081,148 vs 146,105,772, wasm_ir_run 77,378,268 vs 77,402,892 —
# which is the evidence for the host-independence claim above, and why an
# off-CI re-baseline is comparable at all.
#
# Note the two tiers: the three drivers at 6-7 MB link a front-end slice only,
# while the rest sit at 78-161 MB. A 6 MB driver moving 5% is
# 300 KB and means something different from the tracked artifact moving 5%; the
# percentage is what is compared, deliberately, so a small driver's regression is
# not lost inside a big one's noise.

fern.fern 160697188
asm_load_run.fern 152977452
asm_modload_run.fern 150927860
asm_ir_run.fern 150468204
asm_run.fern 149625532
wasm_ir_run.fern 81769324
